title: Midshift SRE catchup and followups
body:
Quick midshift scratchpad - logging things for handoff and follow-ups. Mostly bullety, TODOs, and partially-complete runbook edits (will clean up later).

SUMMARY (TL;DR)
- Pager at 02:18 UTC, widespread 503s hitting hosted inference fleet region-us-west1 for ~17m with sporadic p50/p95 spikes afterward.
- Root cause: KV cache eviction storm + spike in long seq tokenization causing OOM on a subset of serving nodes (notes below).
- Immediate mitigation: scale replica pool + temporarily lower max-batch size on model-prod-2; cold-start throttling for large requests enabled.
- Follow-ups tracked in INFRA-3421 and INC-2026-0314.

TIMELINE / NOTES (timestamps UTC)
- 02:10 alert: increased 5xx rate from 0.2% -> 6.8%, p95 latency for text-gen ~1200ms (normal ~180ms).
- 02:18 pager: alert severity P1 (oncall triggered). I paged Samir.
- 02:20 initial triage: checked console -> autoscaler had healthy nodes but several nodes showed high RSS and restart churn.
- 02:24 rolled a temporary config: set model-prod-2.max_batch_tokens=4096 -> previous 8192. This reduced batch packing and reduced memory pressure.
- 02:29 enabled transient cold-start throttling flag for region-us-west1 (quick fix, toggle id: toggle-2026-03-16-usw1).
- 02:36 notice: affected nodes still OOMing; identified pattern: requests with sequences > 12k tokens (rare) hitting older quantized model variant which does not manage KV cache well.
- 02:45 scaled pool + added two spare nodes in warm pool (autoscaler triggered but I manually pushed to speed up).
- 03:05 service stabilised; 503s dropped to baseline, latency p95 back to ~220ms but p99 has occasional blips.
- 04:10 follow-up: inspected logs and found a client sending batched-broken payloads (see INC ticket). Reached out to CS for customer contact.

ACTIONS TAKEN (short)
- lowered max_batch_tokens for model-prod-2 (temp).
- toggled cold-start throttling for large sequences.
- scaled warm pool + added 2 nodes.
- created INC-2026-0314 (customer payload causing extremes) and linked to INFRA-3421 for infra changes.

RUNBOOK TODOS / CHANGES (immediate)
- [ ] Add step in Serving Runtime runbook: if 5xx > 5% for >5m and p95 > 800ms -> set max_batch_tokens for affected model family to 4096 and monitor for 10m. (owner: Samir)
- [ ] Add automated rule: detect seq_len > 10k and route to quota-backpressure path instead of default variant. (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Add explicit check for older quantized variants: implement quick health-check endpoint that reports KV cache utilization and ensures discard on startup. (owner: me / eng-serving-runtime)
- [ ] Add runbook snippet: "how to toggle cold-start throttling" with feature flag id and rollback notes. (owner: Rafaela)
- [ ] Add cheaper mitigation: when memory pressure detected on node, temporarily reduce concurrent requests to 1 and drain new connections for 30s (automation idea). (owner: platform-engineering)

FOLLOW-UPS (tracked)
- INFRA-3421: "KV cache eviction storm - mitigation and guardrails" - contains initial playbook and instrumentation work. Priority P1 -> P2 after mitigation. (Samir owns).
- INC-2026-0314: customer payload pattern -> CS outreach + request size limits. (Priya owns).
- small post-incident blameless retro scheduled Fri 2026-03-19 15:00 UTC (invite draft: internal/infra-retros). Add example traces and request IDs to agenda. (Rafaela to draft agenda)

DIAGNOSTIC NOTES / OBSERVATIONS
- Memory profiles show large KV cache churn on nodes that had older runtime (v1.18.2) vs updated runtime (v1.19.0) - suspect bug in older eviction path. Need binary-level diff with Samir.
- Affected requests share: long prompt prefix (system message dumps) + user upload (base64) in same request -> tokenization explosion. Need tokenization safety check earlier in gateway.
- Autoscaler reacted slowly because scaling policy prefers CPU signals; memory pressure not a first-class scaling metric. Queue an infra ticket to add memory-backed scaling triggers.

SHORT-TERM MITIGATIONS (for next 24h)
- Enforce request token limit of 12k on API gateway for hosted tier; soft-fail with 413 + guidance to chunk. (Careful: enterprise customers may need exception)
- Tag older runtime clusters in console so routing policy avoids those for large-seq workloads.
- Run targeted canary rollout for runtime v1.19.0 to remaining nodes overnight.

HANDOFF NOTES (to next shift)
- Status: stable but watch p99 blips.
- Key things to monitor: region-us-west1 p99, KV-cache eviction metrics, node restart count (>3 restarts in 10m escalate).
- If 5xx > 3% again: revert to emergency mode (contact list in runbook) -> set max_batch_tokens=2048 for model family and open immediate postmortem channel #inc-3421.
- Contact points: Samir (pager), Priya (CS), Platform-oncall (pager), Eng oncall (rotation schedule in handbook).

PERSONAL NOTES / TODO (quick list)
- write runbook PR for "toggle cold-start throttling" (small doc + cli examples).
- add instrumentation to show per-variant KV cache hit/eviction rates in Console dashboard.
- follow up with Priya about contacting customer and confirming payload reproduction steps.
- review runtime diff between v1.18.2 and v1.19.0 with Samir (schedule pair debug session).

QUESTIONS / UNCERTAINTIES
- How did this surge happen at 02:10? Is it a single client or a behavioral change in multiple clients? Logs point to one large client but not 100% replicated.
- Should we hard-limit the maximum request tokens at gateway or soft-fail? Tradeoffs: customer experience vs platform stability. Need product input.

LINKS / REFERENCES
- INC-2026-0314 (incident): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-0314
- Infra ticket: INFRA-3421: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-3421
- PR for runtime fix (in progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/618
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01EXAMPL0/p1630000000000000 (see Samir notes)

HANDOFF MESSAGE (short to post in #oncall-handoff at 08:00 local)
- "Midshift: handled USW1 503 storm. Mitigations applied (batch size down, cold-start throttling, added warm nodes). Stable now. Follow-ups: INFRA-3421 + INC-2026-0314. Watch p99 for 12h. Rafaela oncall until 09:00 PDT; reach out to Priya/Samir for infra or customer questions."

-- Rafaela
